pages.text: The dynamical Casimir effect: shake a cavity mirror at twice a mode frequency and real photons are pulled out of the vacuum - parametric amplification of nothing. Here the "photons" are whatever virtual particle the Foam resonates with where you stand.
$(thing)Set$(): Resonance tuning, Modulation depth ε, Cavity quality Q, Drive field.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Mirror drive phase noise: the gain varies by ±2%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): Parametric instability: the photon number runs away; The cavity cannot reach that Q at this temperature; Mirror drive too weak for that modulation depth; Interlock: mirror-drive coils not superconducting (too warm); Field above the critical field: the mirror-drive coils quench.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Harvest rate follows the quanta created per stroke.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Parametric gain: G = εQ/4$(br)Quanta per stroke: N = G²/(1 − G²)$(br)Achievable Q: Q_max ∝ 1/R_s(T)$(br)Critical field: B_c(T) = B_c2(0)·(1 − (T/T_c)²)
